items.text: What is the no-spend challenge? The viral money saving trend that could help you reset your financial habits
items.article: The challenge, which first emerged on TikTok, is starting a conversation about saving cash Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Amid relentless commercial advertising urging continuous purchasing, the viral "no-spend challenge" provides a practical way to resist mindless consumerism. Rather than simply converting the traditional virtue of thriftiness into a social media trend, the movement enables individuals to recognise the impulse triggers that prompt unnecessary purchases, helping them break negative spending cycles. Louise Hill, founder of the pocket money and financial education app GoHenry, describes the trend as an effective way to reset personal finances . She explains, "The no-spend challenge is a financial reset which is when you commit to spending zero money on non-essential items for a set period. "It shows you where you spend your money, so that you take more accountability for your purchases. It creates a really clear categorisation in your mind about what your true ‘needs’ are versus your ‘wants’." Hill also views the practice as a constructive method for developing essential money management skills. She adds, "By learning to prioritise your spending and delaying instant gratification, it’s a really useful way of testing yourself and taking back control. Turning it into a challenge is a fun and interesting way to do it – it’s a more positive way of saving money."

items.article: The NHS has shared information about the certain types of coughs that could mean you're suffering from lung cancer. The symptoms come as journalist and TV presenter Dame Esther Rantzen died from the disease this week Sad news broke this week that Dame Esther Rantzen passed away on 30 September 2026 , aged 86, in the New Forest, England. The renowned journalist and television presenter lost her battle with stage four lung cancer after a three-year fight, having first received her diagnosis in January 2023. With this in mind, we're highlighting the key warning signs of lung cancer that you should never ignore. The NHS shared a post on Instagram eight weeks ago detailing the symptoms of the disease, in recognition of World Lung Cancer Day. The caption read: "If you notice any of these signs and symptoms, contact your GP. "It could be nothing serious, but early diagnosis and treatment of cancer can save lives." The symptoms the post urged people to be vigilant about included a cough lasting three weeks or more, a persistent cough that worsens over time, recurring chest infections, and coughing up blood. It is equally important to be aware of an ache or pain when breathing or coughing, persistent breathlessness or fatigue, and a loss of appetite or unexplained weight loss. Between 33,000 and 35,000 people in the UK lose their lives to lung cancer every year. items.text: Christa Pike: Who are Randy Spivey and Stephen Ferrell? Tennessee woman's lawyers speak out after botched execution
items.article: Christa Pike remains critically ill following an unsuccessful execution in Tennessee, prompting her lawyers to request a review of her case. Legal representatives for Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike confirmed on Thursday that she remains in critical condition and is receiving emergency medical intervention following her unsuccessful execution attempt. Pike was transferred to a medical facility Wednesday evening after Tennessee terminated her execution procedure when two consecutive applications of its lethal injection protocol proved ineffective. Witnesses from the media present at the execution were instructed to vacate the premises while Pike could still be heard “snoring.” Pike, 50, was ready to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in approximately 200 years in connection with the homicide of her former classmate, Colleen Slemmer .
